title: There Is No Genocide in Gaza, and Civilian Deaths or Widespread Destruction Alone Do Not Prove Otherwise
description: When discussing the war in Gaza, one of the most frequent and serious allegations leveled against Israel is that it is committing genocide. Yet genocide is not simply another word for a brutal war, extensive destruction, or a tragically high civilian death toll. It is a narrowly defined crime under international law that requires very specific elements, most importantly the intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a protected group as such. The pivotal starting point for the modern conflict is 1947, when the United Nations adopted Resolution 181, proposing the partition of Mandatory Palestine into independent Jewish and Arab states, with Jerusalem under international administration. Jewish leaders accepted partition, while Palestinian leaders and the surrounding Arab states rejected it. Rather than accept the creation of a Jewish state alongside an Arab one, Arab forces figured they outnumbered the Jews 40 million to 700,000, and they could just kill the Jews and take it all. When that failed spectacularly and resulted in what Palestinians remember as the “Nakba,” that would be the earliest starting point for the current conflict. Palestinians continued to reject generous proposals for a peaceful resolution to the conflict, most notably and most recently the Olmert Proposal in 2008. Any reasonable person could easily conclude, after reviewing these proposals and the history, that Palestinians have no evidence of any desire for peace. Both of these are terrorist organizations that consistently commit war crimes and crimes against humanity. Both of these organizations use Palestinian civilians as human shields, and both of these organizations employ the use of hostage taking to achieve political objectives. In regards to Hamas, who is the democratically elected governing body of Gaza. They have consistently embedded their military infrastructure in schools, hospitals, religious sites, historical sites, UN facilities, civilian housing, and other civilian infrastructure. They have poured billions of dollars of foreign aid into developing this terror network deeply within the civilian population. Hamas’s deliberate strategy is to ensure that they cannot be militarily targeted without massive devastation to Palestinian infrastructure and the population. However, this is easily disproven given the fact that Israel has returned land for peace numerous times. Israel gave Jordan and Egypt control of Gaza and the West Bank in exchange for peace after the Arab Israeli War in 1948. Israel returned the Sinai in exchange for peace after the Six-Day War in 1982.
